title: Classify the failed reviewer reset attempt without replay or identity exposure
acceptance: the owner-only command is accepted only on release issue 3072 and is fixed to failed reset run 31706325376

the classifier requires the active REG.RU API and Web revisions to match each other, remain unchanged throughout inspection and be an ancestor of exact diagnostic main; source revision 7c768ad7c54523837b06999a8f69bdffe2a840db must also remain an ancestor
the classifier resolves the unique reviewer only inside the API process through existing confined SECURITY DEFINER functions and never publishes reviewer email or user id
AUTH_DATABASE_URL must be present, isolated from DATABASE_URL and bound to a non-superuser non-BYPASSRLS NOINHERIT principal with existing read-only auth authority

only aggregate challenge and audit counts internally bound to the resolved reviewer user id or keyed account hash for 2026-08-13T13:43:10Z through 2026-08-13T13:43:26Z plus current aggregate readiness and challenge status may be published

the classifier discovers stopped and running Web containers only within the active compose project, skips never-started containers, and reads the bounded source-revision log stream exactly once only when exactly one Web container labeled 7c768ad7c54523837b06999a8f69bdffe2a840db has a Docker lifecycle overlapping the fixed attempt window; multiple matches or an unreadable matching log fail closed

when no lifecycle-bound source-revision Web container remains after the exact release, the classifier publishes UNAVAILABLE_AFTER_EXACT_RELEASE and durable database or audit classes only; Web cardinalities and classes are published as NA or UNAVAILABLE rather than evidence that no terminal event occurred

when the historical log source exists, attributable events are internally bound to the reviewer account hash and a valid correlation id, an unbindable configuration event fails closed, and only cardinalities plus whitelist-derived classes may be published
reviewer identity, account hash, correlation id, reset token or hash, database URLs, credentials, raw rows, raw reasons and raw runtime logs must never be published
no reset request, HTTP auth call, password change, MFA or session change, mail send, database write, privilege change, deployment or container lifecycle operation is performed
SSH accepts exactly one host key matching the protected SHA-256 fingerprint and keeps StrictHostKeyChecking=yes
production mutation is NONE and new recurring cost remains 0 RUB
